page: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the arm64 architecture and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core allocation ratio. It contains no onboard GPUs and does not come provisioned with local ephemeral disk storage, requiring network-attached remote block storage for operating system and data volumes.

The instance is part of the Epsv7 family, supporting Premium Storage connectivity over the network to manage read and write operations. Because the underlying processor utilizes the 64-bit ARM instruction set, software binaries and container runtime dependencies must target arm64 architecture. The absence of integrated local storage means data-intensive operations rely strictly on the attached remote volume performance and throughput limits.

With 32.0 GB of memory allocated across 4 dedicated cores, the instance targets memory-bound workloads that do not demand x86 instruction compatibility or local hardware caching tiers. Common deployments include in-memory databases, caching engines, distributed memory stores, medium-scale relational databases, and ARM-native web and application services.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture and deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature graphical processing hardware or bundled local disk storage, instead utilizing external Premium Storage connectivity for block storage operations. By leveraging dedicated ARM-based compute cores alongside a substantial memory footprint, the instance delivers high resource density for memory-sensitive environments. Because it lacks local solid-state drives, all persistent and swap space depends on attached remote storage volumes. This hardware composition is structured for memory-heavy enterprise tasks, including relational database management systems, in-memory key-value caching layers, data processing pipelines, and microservices compiled for 64-bit ARM environments.
